title: gf2-core PPC-spiral performance sweep
description:
Comprehensive sweep through every scalar gap in `gf2-core` using the Aalto PPC optimization spiral, with proof-of-gain at every step. Each new SIMD kernel lives behind the existing `OnceLock` dispatch boundary in `gf2-kernels-simd`; all high-level code stays `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`. ## Background Phase-1 exploration confirmed three classes of state in `gf2-core`: 1. Already SIMD-accelerated via `OnceLock` dispatch: bitwise XOR/AND/OR/popcount (AVX2), `Fp<65537>` and `Fp<2^31-1>` batch ops, single-shot CLMUL and 4×4 wide CLMUL (VPCLMULQDQ on YMM). 2. Already parallel via rayon: `compute/cpu.rs` row-parallel M4RM/RREF/rank. 3. Scalar gaps with obvious SIMD shape — the targets of this epic. The epic walks the canonical PPC spiral (V0 measure → V1 linearise → V2 ILP → V3 SIMD → V4 register tile → V4cache cache block → V5 reuse → V6 prefetch → V7 layout → V10 multithread). V11 GPU offload is out of scope for `gf2-core` — HIP work lives in `gf2-kernels-hip`. The work is organised into six stories: - **Infrastructure** — pin baselines, compare harness, asm-artefact convention, proptest scaffolding (must land before any tier). - **Dispatch routing** — Tier A: route scalar callers through existing SIMD dispatch (V0→V3 in one hop). - **Dense bit-matrix kernels** — Tier B: new SIMD kernels for transpose, M4RM table build, M4RM block multiply. - **Field-arithmetic batch** — Tier C: GF($2^m$) batch, `Fp

` Montgomery batch, extension-field SoA. - **Sparse layout** — Tier D: prefetch + block-CSR + Cuthill-McKee. - **Multithread** — Tier E: rayon scaling for kernels that are not memory-bound after single-thread tuning. The full per-kernel execution protocol (V0 baseline → asm artefact → perf-stat → proptest equivalence → $\geq 1.5\times$ geomean → commit → lead-only gate transitions) is documented in the epic's spec doc at `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`. ## Success Criteria - [hard] Every Tier A–D kernel ships a criterion bench, sibling `*.asm.txt` artefact, scalar-vs-SIMD proptest equivalence, and $\geq 1.5\times$ geomean over the pinned baseline at the kernel's design size class. - [hard] `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --release --profile ci` passes at fast tier (5 s/test cap). - [hard] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean. - [hard] No `unsafe` leaked outside `gf2-kernels-simd` (`#![deny(unsafe_code)]` preserved everywhere else). - [hard] MSRV stays at 1.80 unless explicitly user-approved per `escalation-policy.md`. - [aspirational] Geomean speedup across all Tier A–D kernels $\geq 2\times$ over the baseline. ## Notes Spec doc with full kernel inventory and per-step protocol: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`. Existing dispatch pattern: `gf2_core::simd::maybe_simd()`, `maybe_gf2m()`, `maybe_mersenne()`, `maybe_fp65537()`, `maybe_gf2m_wide256()` all return `Option<&'static FnsStruct>` via `OnceLock`. New kernels follow the same pattern. Recent baseline data lives under `target/criterion/` (Apr 18–25, 2026); Infrastructure story I1 pins it. ## User-approved closure amendment Approved at epic closure: the original hard success criteria are interpreted through the child-level empirical amendments and no-go evidence recorded during execution. - Sparse layout Tier D retains the delivered block-CSR / RCM / prefetch scaffolds and evidence even where measured kernels did not meet the original >=1.5x target; those outcomes are accepted as documented no-go/negative benchmark results rather than failed correctness work. - Dense multithread Tier E is accepted with `1f899836` rejected under the mandatory memory-bound pre-flight rule and SoA extension-field batching delivered by `10ba5d08`. - Strassen/algorithmic benchmark-gap work is accepted with the production path remaining M4RM-only after measured no crossover through n=8192. - The MSRV criterion is updated from the original Rust 1.80 wording to the current user-approved Rust 1.95 project baseline.

documents.label: PPC-spiral performance plan (full kernel inventory + per-step protocol)
